psnr

A thin R interface to SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl, the distance-based sampling procedure for cognitive social structures data (Feltham, Forastiere & Christakis 2025, Nature Human Behaviour, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-025-02221-6).

The R side only passes data to Julia through JuliaCall. The logic lives in the Julia package; inst/julia/psn_shim.jl translates R data frames and vectors into its arguments.

Installation

Requires Julia 1.10 or later on the PATH, and the R package JuliaCall.

remotes::install_github("emfeltham/psnr")
psnr::psn_setup()

psn_setup() creates a Julia environment of its own (under tools::R_user_dir("psnr", "data")) and installs SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl and its dependencies into it on the first run, which takes a few minutes. Your global Julia environment is not touched. To use a local copy of the Julia package instead of the GitHub version, run psn_setup(pkg = "path/to/SamplingPerceivedNetworks"). The other functions call psn_setup() for you in later sessions.

Usage 

library(psnr)

edges <- data.frame(from = as.character(1:20), to = as.character(c(2:20, 1)))

lists <- psn_sample(edges, seed = 1)   # lists of real and counterfactual pairs
probs <- psn_inclusion_probs(edges)    # exact inclusion probabilities; weight = 1 / pi

See vignette("psnr") for a worked example (custom designs, consents, weights) and ?psn_sample for the arguments. The method itself (orbits, bins, carry-over, consent rules) is documented with the Julia package: https://human-nature-lab.github.io/SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl.
